scenario.disclaimer: Constructed low-fare stress scenario, not observed HK Express prices or budgets. The original flight inventory and NHPP quota are held fixed; NHPP is not reforecast for the assumed normal fare. A zero promotional quote does not override the independent revenue-adoption decision.

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 7 bought at the 48 HKD member fare and 25 declined. Most declines (19) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection. Four declines cited low interest or recent travel with a strong outside option, and two of those explicitly said the 12 HKD saving was not compelling. Buyers called 48 HKD a genuinely low fare; several would still pay 60 HKD. The current price already equals the 48 HKD cap, so no higher test is permitted.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 48 HKD fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly one-fifth conversion, with most declines driven by budget or inventory constraints rather than fare level; a materially different conversion rate would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 48 member fare, 10 of 32 customers bought and 22 declined. Most declines (18) cite no ticket both available and within budget, an inventory/budget constraint rather than a fare objection; three declines cite low trip interest or a strong outside option, and one buyer would not pay the HKD 60 regular fare. Several buyers say they would still buy at HKD 60. The fare is at its permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 48 fare on fresh customers will reproduce roughly 30% weighted conversion; if a fresh paired sample shows materially lower conversion with no change in inventory denials, the current-fare retention assumption is contradicted.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: At HKD 48 the member fare is a genuinely cheap escape, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 6 bought the HK$48 member fare and 26 declined. Most declines (21) were environment-forced: no offered ticket was both available and within the basic-fare budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection. Four declines cited low trip interest and a strong outside option despite finding HK$48 affordable. Buyers described the fare as a compelling low price; three would also pay the HK$60 regular fare. The current price already equals the permitted cap of 48.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher fare is impossible since HK$48 is the cap. A fresh paired test at the same fare should show whether the 21 environment-forced declines persist; if they do, the constraint is inventory/budget, not price, and conversion will not respond to fare changes.

analysis.summary: At the current 48 HKD member fare, 10 of 32 customers bought, all citing the low fare as the decisive trigger; several said they would not pay the 60 HKD normal fare. Most declines (18) were environment-forced, reporting no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection. Two declines cited low trip interest or recent travel. The fare is already at its permitted cap, so no higher test is possible; evidence points to holding the capped fare.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 48 HKD capped member fare on fresh customers will reproduce roughly 30% weighted conversion, with most non-buyers declining for availability/budget constraints rather than explicit price objections; materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At HKD 47, 9 of 32 members bought, generating HKD 423 in basic receipts. Most declines (20) were environment-forced, meaning no offered ticket was both available and within budget, not a price objection. Two declines cited low interest and a strong outside option despite finding HKD 47 affordable. Buyers repeatedly called the fare compelling and several would decline at HKD 60. The low fare appears to drive conversion, but no decline is a genuine price objection, so a lower-price direction is unsupported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 47 member fare on fresh customers will reproduce weighted conversion near 0.28; a materially lower conversion would contradict retaining the fare, while a materially higher one would suggest headroom to test a higher fare.

analysis_attempts.error: A lower-price hypothesis needs a cited decline and a reported price objection

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The paired initial at HKD 48 produced only 4 member buyers and far lower revenue, suggesting the current fare is effective. Evidence supports testing the same fare on fresh customers rather than raising it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 32 member fare on fresh paired customers will preserve conversion near the observed level; a materially lower conversion would contradict retaining this fare, while higher fares are untested here.

analysis.summary: At HKD 39, 12 of 32 members bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain; 13 declines were inventory/budget-forced and 4 were low-interest optional-trip declines. No customer objected to price as too high. The current fare sits below the HKD 48 cap, and several buyers said they would decline at the HKD 60 regular fare. Evidence supports testing a higher member fare on fresh customers, though buying at 39 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh paired customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus HKD 39, because no supplied decline cited price as too high and several buyers named a budget ceiling above 39.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 43, ten members bought and all cited the low fare as compelling; several said they would not pay the HKD 60 normal fare. Most declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections, and a few declined for low destination appeal or recent travel. No customer objected to the fare itself. The current fare sits below the HKD 48 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough member purchases that basic-ticket receipts exceed those at HKD 43, since buyers cited the fare as a bargain rather than a hard ceiling.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Most buyers cite the HKD 41 member fare as a compelling bargain that converts casual browsing into a booking; several would also pay the HKD 60 regular fare. Declines split between environment-forced unavailability and low-interest/recent-travel customers who find the fare affordable but the trip not worthwhile. analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts enough to offset the higher per-ticket revenue, because most current buyers cite the fare as compelling and several accept the HKD 60 regular fare.

The current price sits below the HKD 48 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 37 member fare, 11 of 32 customers bought, generating HKD 407 in basic receipts; 19 declined, nearly all citing no ticket both available and within budget. Buyers repeatedly describe the fare as a compelling bargain, and several say they would not pay the HKD 60 normal fare. The cap is HKD 48, so a higher test is permitted. Evidence suggests low price drives conversion, but declines are budget/availability framed rather than explicit price objections.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic receipts, because most buyers cite strong bargain appeal and several would decline at HKD 60; if conversion falls enough to lower total receipts, the hypothesis is contradicted.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 33, 18 of 32 customers bought the member fare, mostly citing it as a compelling bargain below their budget ceilings. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and five were low-interest optional-trip declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Several buyers said they would not pay the HKD 60 regular fare, while a few would. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 33 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh paired customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts versus HKD 33, because most buyers cited budget ceilings well above the current fare and no customer objected to price.

analysis.summary: At HKD 34, 18 of 32 members bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain within their budgets; most would decline the HKD 60 regular fare. Nine declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available ticket, and two were low-interest optional-trip refusals. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current price sits below the HKD 48 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus HKD 34, since buyers cited budgets well above the current fare and several would pay HKD 60.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 29, 20 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing its low price as the decisive trigger; most said they would decline at HKD 60. Nine declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were low-interest optional-trip refusals despite affordability. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current price sits well below the HKD 48 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will keep conversion high enough that base-ticket receipts exceed those at HKD 29, since most buyers cited the fare as a bargain well under their stated budgets.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.

Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.

Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
